title: React Module 07 Applied Check
description: Apply Hooks concepts to dependency arrays, cleanup, stale closures, refs, memoization, context updates, reducers, and Hook rule mistakes.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: What is wrong with `if (enabled) { const [count, setCount] = useState(0); }`?

options.text: It calls a Hook conditionally
`useState` cannot store numbers
The variable name is too long
Hooks must be async

questions.explanation: Hooks must be called in the same order on every render, so conditions go inside Hook logic, not around Hook calls.

questions.prompt: An effect subscribes to `roomId` changes. Which are usually needed? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Include `roomId` in the dependency array
Return cleanup that unsubscribes from the old room
Leave the dependency array empty so it never changes
Keep subscription side effects out of render

questions.explanation: Effects should list changing values they use and clean up subscriptions before rerunning or unmounting.

questions.prompt: Which value should go in an effect dependency array?

options.text: Reactive values from props, state, or component scope that the effect reads
Only literal strings
Only values from package.json
Nothing, dependencies are optional style

questions.explanation: Dependencies describe the reactive values the effect uses so React can rerun it when needed.

questions.prompt: Updating `ref.current` causes React to re-render the component.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Refs are mutable containers that do not schedule renders when changed.

options.text: For an expensive derived calculation whose dependencies change less often
For every simple string concatenation
To run side effects after render
To replace all local variables

questions.explanation: Memoization has overhead and is most useful for expensive calculations or identity-sensitive values.

questions.prompt: Which are common `useCallback` pitfalls? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Omitting dependencies used by the callback
Using it everywhere without a reason
Expecting it to make the function body faster
Pairing it with memoized children when function identity matters

questions.explanation: `useCallback` stabilizes identity, not execution speed. It still needs correct dependencies and a reason.

questions.prompt: A reducer directly mutates state and returns the same object. What is the issue?

options.text: Reducers should be pure and return new state objects for changes
Reducers must always fetch data
Reducers cannot handle objects
Actions cannot have types

questions.explanation: Reducer logic should be pure and immutable so React can detect and reason about updates.

questions.prompt: Which statements about context are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Consumers re-render when the provider value they read changes
Context is useful for avoiding prop drilling for shared values
Context is automatically a full server cache
Provider value identity can matter for unnecessary renders

questions.explanation: Context shares values through the tree, but it is not a data-fetching cache and updates can re-render consumers.
